title: Je parle, tu parles…
intro: About 9 out of 10 French verbs end in **-er**, and almost all of them follow the same pattern. Learn it once and you can use hundreds of verbs: *parler, aimer, habiter, cuisiner, regarder…*

cases.label: je … -e
cases.rule: **je** + stem + **-e**: *je parle*. Before a vowel or silent h, **je → j'**: *j'aime, j'habite*.

cases.label: il / elle / on … -e
cases.rule: **il, elle, on** + stem + **-e**: *il parle, on parle*.

cases.label: ils / elles … -ent
cases.rule: **ils, elles** + stem + **-ent**: *ils parlent*. The **-ent** is silent!

cases.label: four forms, one sound
cases.rule: *je parle, tu parles, il parle, ils parlent* all sound /paʁl/. Only **nous** (-ons) and **vous** (-ez) sound different.

cases.label: verbs starting with a vowel
cases.rule: **nous‿aimons, vous‿habitez, ils‿aiment**: you hear a /z/. That's how you hear *il aime* /i.lɛm/ vs *ils aiment* /il.zɛm/.

cases.label: one present = three English tenses
cases.rule: *Je regarde* = I watch / I'm watching / I do watch. French has no “-ing” form: never “je suis regardant”.

cases.label: negatives and questions
cases.rule: **ne … pas** around the verb (*je ne parle pas*, *je n'aime pas*). Questions: voice up, or **est-ce que**: *Est-ce que tu parles anglais ?*

sections.title: 1. The pattern: stem + ending
text: Take the infinitive, remove **-er** to get the stem (*parler → parl-*), then add the ending for each person.

sections.title: 3. Four forms, one sound
text: The endings **-e, -es, -e, -ent** are all silent, so four forms sound exactly the same. Only **nous** and **vous** sound different.

examples.en: He speaks French and they speak English.

sections.tip: So in speech, *il parle* and *ils parlent* sound the same — the rest of the sentence tells you which one it is.

sections.title: 4. Verbs starting with a vowel
text: **je → j'**: *j'aime, j'habite, j'écoute*. With **nous, vous, ils, elles** you hear a /z/ link: *nous‿aimons, vous‿habitez, ils‿aiment*. Here you CAN hear the plural: *il aime* /i.lɛm/, *ils‿aiment* /il.zɛm/.

sections.title: 5. One present, three English tenses
text: *Je regarde la télé* can mean **I watch TV**, **I'm watching TV** or **I do watch TV**. French has no separate “-ing” form.

examples.fr: {Je regarde|er-meaning} la télé tous les soirs.

sections.tip: Never translate “I am watching” word for word: not *je suis regardant*, just **je regarde**.

sections.title: 6. Saying no and asking questions
text: **ne** before the verb, **pas** after it: *je ne parle pas*. Before a vowel: *je n'aime pas*.
Questions: raise your voice (*Tu parles anglais ?*) or put **est-ce que** in front (*Est-ce que tu parles anglais ?*).

mistakes.why: The **-ent** of a verb is silent.
No “-ing” form in French: **je regarde** = I'm watching.

story.title: Dimanche chez les grands-parents
story.en: The whole family has Sunday lunch at Jacques and Louise's house.

lines.fr: Le dimanche, toute la famille {déjeune|er-il} chez Jacques et Louise.
lines.en: On Sundays, the whole family has lunch at Jacques and Louise's.

lines.fr: Dans la cuisine, Louise {prépare|er-il} un poulet.
lines.en: In the kitchen, Louise is cooking a chicken.

lines.fr: Léa, {tu épluches|er-tu} les pommes de terre ?
lines.en: Léa, will you peel the potatoes?

lines.fr: Oui ! Et Hugo, {il coupe|er-il} les carottes.
lines.en: Yes! And Hugo is cutting the carrots.

lines.fr: Non, moi, {je regarde|er-meaning} le match à la télé !
lines.en: No, I'm watching the match on TV!

lines.fr: Hugo ! {Nous préparons|er-nous} le déjeuner ensemble. Tu aides !
lines.en: Hugo! We're making lunch together. You're helping!

lines.fr: Dans le salon, Paul et Jacques {parlent|er-ils}. {Ils écoutent|er-liaison} de la musique.
lines.en: In the living room, Paul and Jacques are talking. They're listening to music.
Karim, are you still working at the restaurant?

lines.fr: Lou {joue|er-il} avec le chien sous la table.
lines.en: Lou is playing with the dog under the table.

lines.fr: Tout le monde {aime|er-sound} le poulet de Louise, et {les enfants adorent|er-sound} les desserts de Karim.
lines.en: Everyone loves Louise's chicken, and the children love Karim's desserts.

lines.fr: Merci, mon chéri. Mais {tu ne manges pas|er-neg-q} tes carottes ?
lines.en: Thank you, darling. But aren't you eating your carrots?

lines.fr: Euh… {je n'aime pas|er-neg-q} les carottes cuites !
lines.en: Um… I don't like cooked carrots!

lines.fr: Après le repas, Paul et Hugo {lavent|er-ils} la vaisselle, et Louise {regarde|er-sound} les photos avec Léa.
lines.en: After the meal, Paul and Hugo do the dishes, and Louise looks at photos with Léa.

lines.fr: Pourquoi {je lave|er-je} toujours la vaisselle, moi ?
lines.en: Why am I always the one doing the dishes?

quiz.q: Which forms sound exactly the same?
options: je parle, tu parles, il parle, ils parlent
quiz.answer: je parle, tu parles, il parle, ils parlent
quiz.say: je parle, tu parles, il parle, ils parlent

quiz.q: How do you pronounce « ils regardent » ?
« Je regarde la télé » can mean…
options: I watch TV / I'm watching TV
quiz.answer: I watch TV / I'm watching TV
